9ccfb6a68585.title: Language Models for Text Classification: From Bag-of-Words to Jev
9ccfb6a68585.author: Sebastian Raschka, PhD
9ccfb6a68585.description: A Visual Guide to RNNs, CNNs, Transformers, and Calibration, with Hands-On Experiments on Accuracy and Efficiency
9ccfb6a68585.summary: The recently released Jev AI model has been quite a cultural phenomenon in technical communities in the past 2 weeks. While Jev aims to classify things, it’s easy to dismiss Jev as “just a classifier,” and my own view of Jev has evolved quite a bit over the past few days.
takeaways: Sure, the latest state-of-the-art GPT and open-weight LLMs can do the same kinds of classification tasks as Jev, while also being capable of much more general decision-making.
However, I thought starting with a brief history of language models for decision-making would be a great way to begin.
Language modeling and classification in the pre-transformer era For completeness, before we put Jev in context (no pun intended), I thought it made the most sense to start chronologically.

987754dece67.title: Meta shakes up the frontiers, open and closed
987754dece67.author: Nathan Lambert
987754dece67.summary: This has been a week where the balance of American open-weight models took a step change back toward the frontier. Meta took the lead of this charge with Muse Spark Open , which is now the strongest American-made open model by quite some margin, but the addition of Reflection’s first model Beam is also relevant.
takeaways: The inference providers are rapidly scaling, the open post-training economy is forming, and countless enterprises are looking to own their intelligence.
When Meta released Muse Glimmer , the 30B agentic model, Alex Wang said that they were preparing to release the Muse Spark 1.2 model as open weights, which fits with the above.
Riding off a rapid increase in performance of Chinese models, the open ecosystem has been living through an acceleration in demand.

992438874f53.title: I expect rapid progress but not towards general superintelligence
992438874f53.author: Nathan Lambert
992438874f53.description: I’ve often been surprised when I hear from top researchers in industry that they think AI will be better than them at their job in a few years, and I didn’t really know why I doubted it.
992438874f53.summary: I’ve often been surprised when I hear from top researchers in industry that they think AI will be better than them at their job in a few years, and I didn’t really know why I doubted it. The explanation I arrived at is that researchers are seeing this massive acceleration in the infra and engineering capabilities of the models.
takeaways: A lot of this near-term progress comes from scaling the inference-time compute we have with current tools, rather than dramatic step-changes in how good the models are at research.
Inference metrics look like tokens per prompt, FLOPs per token, or really just cost per answer.
A prediction of pretraining research, at least in architecture and data selection to serve our current class of models, being automated in 2-3 years feels reasonable to me.

ee5a948a7c39.title: The Cyber Risk Discourse is Broken
ee5a948a7c39.author: Nathan Lambert
ee5a948a7c39.summary: I feel like we’re locked in on a path of lose-lose situation, unless people embrace nuance, trade-offs, and scary realities. Much has been written about the views of various players in this debate, which I summarize as follows: Open weight models pose an untenable risk to society’s functionality , occupied by frontier lab leadership and the national security community in the U.S.
takeaways: Chinese companies continuing to release open-weight models with strong cyber capabilities , who are making decisions based on the risk assessments of their society and government.

This sort of solipsistic writing by Anthropic fits very closely to another type of discourse I’m hearing about regularly that is determining the fate of open models and AI broadly — classified briefings.

I may agree with the simple reality that closed models are far safer in the limit, as a technical tool with more layers of protection, but they may actually be causing more harm in the near term because of how accessible model APIs are.

9a319be2f748.title: The current balance of power in open models

9a319be2f748.description: The expanded form of a testimony I prepared for Congress.
9a319be2f748.summary: I was recently invited to brief a group of Congressional members and staff on the state of open-weight models in the lens of U.S.-China competition. I’m sharing my prepared remarks as a state of the union on open models that is accessible to a broader audience.
takeaways: Closed models offer access only through Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) that developers can use to directly query a model, like GPT-4 or Claude Opus 4.5, or through products, like ChatGPT and Claude Code.

These models are governed by licenses, governing documents dictating what is allowed with downstream use, and are often accompanied by inference code in libraries such as Transformers, VLLM, SGLANG, etc.
The Chinese labs release their models faster and focus on a slightly narrower distribution of tasks, flattering them slightly on public benchmarks.

This cultural precondition, when exposed to the reality that thousands of agents will constantly be working fairly productively in your business, will only increase this anxiety.

e723d856f72c.title: One resignation turned the embers of AI fear into a wildfire
e723d856f72c.author: Nathan Lambert
e723d856f72c.description: Some quick notes on a truly weird week.
e723d856f72c.summary: As AI became more powerful, it was inevitable that a different, growing group would start to take AI safety more seriously – what we did not know ahead of time, is which set of views they latched onto. We have seen that some of the most extreme views of risk, i.e. moderate probabilities of mass extinction, were the ones that reached the masses.
takeaways: As the stakes of AI have risen this year, from the OpenAI-HuggingFace incident and breakthroughs like the Navier-Stokes result (also from OpenAI), the ground has dried out and the latent energy around the AI discourse has increased.
I say this without blaming individuals, but it’s a common agreement among my friends not at OpenAI/Anthropic (Ant especially) that people at the labs operate with a religious energy.
The entire discourse around existential risk is on very poor footing.

2a3a8c33e461.summary: Reasoning over long document contexts remains a challenge for large language models (LLMs). Standard retrieval methods are inherently reactive, bottlenecking agents with complex, cross-document reasoning at inference time, while precomputed structures like knowledge graphs often fall short because they rely on rigid heuristics.
takeaways: Standard retrieval methods are inherently reactive, bottlenecking agents with complex, cross-document reasoning at inference time, while precomputed structures like knowledge graphs often fall short because they rely on rigid heuristics.

We build on a key asymmetry in modern agentic harnesses (e.g., Claude Code): while LLM agents are adept at navigating existing filesystems to solve an immediate task, they are rarely trained to construct reusable workspaces for future use.

Empirically, Librarian Agents outperforms the strongest retrieval and precomputation baselines by 33 percentage points on BrowseComp-Plus, amortizes upfront construction costs across repeated queries, and generalizes zero-shot to unseen domains on BRIGHT with a 31-point average accuracy improvement.

takeaways: Agents flatten these semantics, so injected text can persuade the LLM to exercise the user's authority for content that has none.
As LLMs remain easy to persuade, the agent's interface to the web must itself ensure the integrity of what the agent reads, interprets, and does.
Intact passes the page via GenTree to the LLM one element at a time, so the LLM decides on each element without any other element's text.

345e1296312e.summary: Multi-object tracking in sports broadcasts is hard for two reasons: athletes move fast and change direction abruptly, and the camera pans and zooms at the same time. We present ARC-SORT (Adaptive, Robust, Compensated SORT), a tracking-by-detection tracker that trains nothing and runs in real time.
takeaways: An Interacting Multiple Model (IMM) Kalman filter gives every track a predictive covariance, and we turn it into a per-track search region: the less reliable the motion prediction, the larger the region in which a detection may match (uncertainty-adaptive Expansion IoU, EIoU).
When two tracks cross, the assignment cost itself reports whether the decision was close.

ARC-SORT keeps such pairs under review and applies at most one corrective identity swap once post-crossing appearance evidence shows the first decision was wrong; this adds +1.0 HOTA (higher order tracking accuracy) on both the SportsMOT and DanceTrack test sets at under a millisecond per frame.

takeaways: Because each latent decodes to a mask, the model can interleave reasoning with region-specific latents and thus think with visual latents, while grounded reasoning traces supervise the regions it visits during chain-of-thought.

As a result, across all eight RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg splits, Xiaomi-Lens-0 gains 5.6 points on average over Qwen3.5 in referring comprehension and achieves the highest segmentation cIoU among compared models.

Distillation provides a promising way for a student model to learn from a teacher's dynamics, enabling one-step or few-step generation.
In this work, we propose Consistent Distribution Matching, a simulation-free and data-free distillation method for accelerating diffusion and flow models while preserving strong generative capacity.

5900036f68de.author: Sai Kiran Bathula
5900036f68de.description: In a small language model the vocabulary is the single largest part. 5900036f68de.summary: In a small language model the vocabulary is the single largest part. In Gemma 3 270M the embedding table holds 168M of 268M parameters, and because quantisation methods leave the embedding in 16-bit, it is also most of the file once the rest of the model is compressed.
takeaways: With a ternary BitNet b1.58 body the whole model is a 46 MB file, still ties the float model on LAMBADA and PIQA, and on a laptop CPU generates 615 to 740 tokens per second in 62 MB of memory, five to six times the speed of the float model's 8-bit GGUF in llama.cpp at a seventh of the memory.

In Gemma 3 270M the embedding table holds 168M of 268M parameters, and because quantisation methods leave the embedding in 16-bit, it is also most of the file once the rest of the model is compressed.

We replace it with one frozen table of 512-bit codes, 16 MB, with no trainable parameters, derived once from a pretrained embedding by principal-component projection and sign binarisation, and we train the same Gemma-shaped body from scratch on the same 2.05B tokens with and without it.

takeaways: The corpus serves both inference and training: PosterRAG, a training-free multi-agent pipeline, retrieves an exemplar and refills its slots without touching layout or styling, while an SFT+RL recipe trains a dedicated model from the same triplets.

RAP contains 25K+ verified paper-poster pairs from various machine learning conferences held between 2022 and 2026, annotated with a three-level content taxonomy, plus a held-out benchmark of 150 test papers each paired with its human poster.
We introduce RAP (Reconstruct A Poster), a dataset and benchmark for paper-to-poster generation as a visual coding task.

takeaways: These results show that persistent evidence and prospective reasoning can improve recovery in long-horizon agent tasks while substantially reducing reliance on teacher-model inference.

takeaways: OPMD achieves the highest average accuracy among the evaluated distillation baselines in all three teacher--student settings, and generalizes to multi-teacher distillation and cross-family supervised fine-tuning.

e1299b9c5dca.author: Jian Gu, Hongyu Zhang, Chunyang Chen, Aldeida Aleti
e1299b9c5dca.description: The vocabulary of a language model is its native semantics: the embedding and the unembedding fix the meaning of a state at the two ends of the residual stream. Between them, existing methods either reuse a fixed lens or treat the states as a point cloud, and neither reads a state the way the model does. We argue that…
e1299b9c5dca.summary: The vocabulary of a language model is its native semantics: the embedding and the unembedding fix the meaning of a state at the two ends of the residual stream. Between them, existing methods either reuse a fixed lens or treat the states as a point cloud, and neither reads a state the way the model does.
takeaways: Lexical reference frames approximate it by reading a state through the model's own remaining layers with a stated number of rounds of attention between positions and a typical attention output for the rest, without fitting to the model's output.

No lens, with fixed directions per layer, can exceed the square root of the native frame's coherence, 0.30 and 0.35 at mid-depth of SmolLM3-3B and OLMo3-7B, whereas the first-order frame, LexFrame[1], reaches 0.97 and 0.97 and reads a state within 0.16 nats of the model's output.

Its coefficients attribute predictions more faithfully than attribution patching, its lexical basis steers a prediction while sparing other tokens, and its confident readings would let an early exit skip 0.45 and 0.42 of the layers, where lenses skip almost none.

a22a6ca92e5c.description: We’re launching a new, expanded version of our Cyber Verification Program (CVP), which makes advanced cyber capabilities and reduced blocking classifiers available to qualifying security professionals.
a22a6ca92e5c.summary: We’re launching a new, expanded version of our Cyber Verification Program (CVP), which makes advanced cyber capabilities and reduced blocking classifiers available to qualifying security professionals. The program now consists of three access tiers, which allow security teams to apply for the level of access that best suits their work.
takeaways: Testing the efficacy of our tiers To assess the efficacy of our CVP protections, we ran Claude Opus 5.5 through CyScenarioBench—an evaluation that measures whether models can plan and execute multi-stage cyber operations under realistic constraints—with safeguards tuned for our different CVP tiers.

Because this evaluation involves complex, interactive offensive scenarios, we would expect Claude to experience significant blocks both on the generally available model and in the Defense Access tier, while experiencing no blocks in the Red Team Access and Specialized Access tiers.
Each tier includes access to our most capable models, including Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Mythos 5.1, and new models moving forward.

8c17f1f1ac30.summary: Updated October 15 to include more detail on the projects that pioneered many of the techniques we use in Scion. At Anthropic, coding is no longer the bottleneck to building systems or doing research.
takeaways: Unsurprisingly, Anthropic uses Claude to write software far more than almost any other company, so we’re often the first to see where tools built for human scale start to strain.

Taking a step back, we noticed that, like most companies, we were using git as a centralized system with one authoritative copy, but nearly all of our clients were agents and jobs that are online by definition.
In May 2026, Anthropic averaged around 2,500 code changes merged per day; as of September, we merged over 30,000 per day.

6102ac4cd82d.summary: A Sensible Default is a practice that, absent some overriding context, should be used when carrying out a certain kind of task. In software development such sensible defaults might include things like “use version control”, “separate UI logic from domain logic”, “automate deployment pipelines”.
takeaways: The term “sensible default” is a deliberate contrast to “best practice”.
Folks dislike calling things “best practice” because that term implies a general presumption that the best practice is something we should always expect to do.
A sensible default is what we'd expect you to do, the practices to apply, if there are no hard constraints in the environment.

takeaways: It started with a series of ​ carefully planned announcements​ and reports from OpenAI that try to establish how unnerving and powerful (not to mention ​felonious​ ) their LLM-powered agent systems have become.

takeaways: They took a relatively common technology called an LLM-powered agent, which is used with minimal issues by millions of software developers every day, and ​then added​ a bunch of dangerous features, removed restrictions, and released a whole mess of them into poorly fenced digital wilds.
Given OpenAI’s interest in an IPO, for example, there might have been pressure to do well on this particular benchmark to establish their model’s power.
So, I thought it would be useful to publish three short follow-up points that summarize my core claims more directly… Point #1: Anthropic and OpenAI are not able to create superintelligent AI.

1341737db773.title: The Best Way to Take Notes
1341737db773.author: Scott Young
1341737db773.description: The best way to take notes may be the method that uses the least technology. I'll explain why notes still matter and how to learn better with them. The post The Best Way to Take Notes appeared first on Scott H Young .
1341737db773.summary: Is there still a point to taking notes these days? When I was in school, the purpose of note-taking was obvious.
takeaways: Note-Taking and Cognitive Load One area I didn’t get a chance to dive into in the video essay was somewhat more “advanced” note-taking strategies, such as mind-maps, linking ideas together, analogies or rephrasing material as retrieval prompts.

Broadly speaking, there’s evidence in favor of handwriting over typing notes out—evidence that becomes stronger, in my opinion, when you add the likelihood of digital distractions that occurs in most real-world situations with digital notes.
But the basic truth seems to be that anything that causes you to really pay attention while you’re sitting in a lecture is going to improve your academic performance.

a2c93cc334d0.description: Effective learning doesn't need to be complicated. Here's a simple trick that outperforms mind-maps. The post The Simple Method That Boosts Memory by 50% appeared first on Scott H Young .
a2c93cc334d0.summary: Sometimes the most powerful methods for learning better are also the simplest. In my latest video essay, I discuss the power of retrieval practice, and explain why students consistently underrate its effectiveness: Are Mind Maps a Waste of Time?
takeaways: Retrieve, Don’t Re-Read Despite these caveats, I think retrieval practice remains one of the most powerful learning strategies to have in your toolkit.

Another objection may be that, by focusing on concept maps made with the book open, the researchers ignored a more beneficial third alternative: that you could combine concept maps with retrieval practice and do better than both!
They found that adding retrieval practice to mind mapping yields the same boost to memory as free recall alone.

5e2df814d903.title: Reach the Top 1% of Your Field (Deliberate Practice)
5e2df814d903.author: Scott Young
5e2df814d903.description: Revisiting one of the most influential theories of mastery and professional excellence. The post Reach the Top 1% of Your Field (Deliberate Practice) appeared first on Scott H Young .
5e2df814d903.summary: Few ideas have shaped my thinking about learning more than Anders Ericsson’s work on deliberate practice. He argued persuasively that quantity of practice goes a long way in explaining performance differences in fields like chess, music and athletics and, further, that certain types of practice are far more effective than others for learning.
takeaways: He argued persuasively that quantity of practice goes a long way in explaining performance differences in fields like chess, music and athletics and, further, that certain types of practice are far more effective than others for learning.

To me, this doesn’t undermine the more basic claims that a large quantity of practice is important for learning and that certain kinds of effortful/guided practice may be much more effective than simply spending hours performing the skill.
If expertise isn’t defined in terms of repeatable, superior performance according to an unbiased standard, then the study shifts from cognitive development to sociology.

546c03dc62cf.title: You Should Care Less About Practical Advice

546c03dc62cf.description: Most readers prefer useful advice to abstract theory. They shouldn't. The post You Should Care Less About Practical Advice appeared first on Scott H Young .
546c03dc62cf.summary: After twenty years of writing, I’ve developed a feel for what my audience wants. I don’t always deliver, but I have, at the very least, a strong intuition whether an essay I write is going to have broad appeal, or mostly be read by a handful of fans.
takeaways: Finally, at the trunk, you get to bedrock ideas about learning like the spacing effect or retrieval practice.

A little further down the tree are basic ideas of entrepreneurship like “product-market fit”, “minimum viable product” and “market research.” And towards the base are fundamental concepts like “supply and demand.” Or consider the topic I write most about: effective learning.
If you care about usefulness, spending most of your time learning “advice” or “tips” is counterproductive.

This enables efficient fine-tuning of multimodal backbones with up to 104B parameters, the largest model adapted for brain encoding to our knowledge.
We show that parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) enables us to effectively adapt very large pretrained backbones for brain encoding with a small number of trainable parameters.

takeaways: We introduce HOLI-WORLD, an integrated ecosystem connecting experience capture, world representation, automated data construction, model learning, and independent evaluation.

Experiments on ScanNet, ScanNet++, Aria Digital Twin, and HOLIWORLD-Bench demonstrate strong performance in static perception and dynamic tracking, while training on HOLIWORLD-Data substantially improves HOLIWORLD-VL-4B's spatial and temporal reasoning on HOLI- WORLD-Bench and EgoDynamic4D.

Realizing this potential at scale requires turning growing volumes of recordings into learning resources that connect scene structure, object semantics, and interaction histories across viewpoints and time, while reducing dependence on costly manual annotation.

takeaways: However, learning through human corrections requires teleoperators to monitor execution and intervene when policies fail, a demand that is difficult to meet as robot fleets grow.
We introduce collective experience learning (CEL), a learning paradigm in which deployed robots share their execution experience to improve a common policy.
Across five real-world manipulation tasks, the resulting policies achieve success rates of 93.3-99.2%, evaluated over 120 trials per task on robots excluded from training data collection.

233627fd273d.summary: Many modern language models have adopted hybrid architectures that incorporate both linear-time recurrence and softmax attention. Modern recurrence layers provide a highly expressive mixing mechanism while ensuring high throughput by compressing contextual information into a fixed-size state, but underperform softmax attention in contextual information retrieval.
takeaways: Empirical results on models up to 1B parameters show that our method results in substantial improvement in language modeling loss, common-sense reasoning, as well as a wide range of retrieval-related tasks across different context lengths.

Modern recurrence layers provide a highly expressive mixing mechanism while ensuring high throughput by compressing contextual information into a fixed-size state, but underperform softmax attention in contextual information retrieval.

Layer attribution analysis reveals that under typical data distributions, modern recurrence learns retrieval functions faster than softmax attention, causing attention to fail to learn retrieval in most cases.

takeaways: Second, we develop an end-to-end text-to-world pipeline that combines semantic scene planning with Deterministic Frustum-Guided Grid Placement to construct large-scale 3D worlds with precise object placement, procedural population, and animation.

Existing methods either access the manga mainly through text, losing its characters and art style, or feed manga pages directly into video generation models, which misinterpret the manga's structure and produce incorrect storylines.
Each representation is produced by a creator agent and reviewed against the source panels by a paired reviewer agent.

takeaways: We present EgoXperience, a full-stack paradigm that addresses these needs through data collection, automatic annotation, unified modeling, and benchmarking.

takeaways: Under such stringent joint constraints, we find that existing lifelong-memory methods can become ineffective, with several sophisticated approaches offering little advantage over simple retrieval or even no-memory agents.

To address this challenge, we propose TokenWorth, a lightweight online memory framework that learns query-dependent memory worth from sparse execution feedback and applies it consistently to memory retrieval and bounded memory management.

a8d376233b1d.title: Any 3D Scene is Worth 1K Tokens: 3D-Grounded Representation for Scene Generation at Scale
a8d376233b1d.author: Dongxu Wei, Qi Xu, Zhiqi Li, Hangning Zhou et al.
a8d376233b1d.description: Scene-level 3D generation has long been dominated by 2D multi-view or video diffusion models. a8d376233b1d.summary: Scene-level 3D generation has long been dominated by 2D multi-view or video diffusion models. Typically, these 2D-based approaches perform scene generation in a 2D latent space, which introduces two fundamental issues: (i) representing 3D scenes via 2D views leads to significant representation redundancy, and (ii) latent space rooted in 2D inherently limits the spatial consistency of the generated scenes.
takeaways: Then we tame diffusion transformers to perform diffusion modeling directly in the 3D latent space, enabling 3D-grounded scene generation.
In this paper, we propose to perform 3D scene generation directly within a high-dimensional implicit 3D latent space derived from powerful 2D foundation models (e.g., DINOv2, SigLIP2, DA3).

In our experiments, we not only demonstrate the advantages of our method over 2D-based approaches in terms of efficiency and spatial consistency, but also comprehensively analyze the impact of 3D latent representation on 3D scene generation performance.

75e579a1c88d.description: While LLM-based agent systems have demonstrated remarkable proficiency in reasoning and solving complex real-world tasks, they also come with substantial token consumption and inference latency, limiting their practical deployment. 75e579a1c88d.summary: While LLM-based agent systems have demonstrated remarkable proficiency in reasoning and solving complex real-world tasks, they also come with substantial token consumption and inference latency, limiting their practical deployment. To enhance the efficiency of agent systems, recent efforts have focused on transferring agentic capabilities from large-scale models to small language models (SLMs) via supervised fine-tun
takeaways: To enhance the efficiency of agent systems, recent efforts have focused on transferring agentic capabilities from large-scale models to small language models (SLMs) via supervised fine-tuning-based distillation.
By iteratively applying this procedure, ProD enables student agents to progressively approximate teacher behavior.

Extensive experiments involving 8 SLMs, ranging from 0.6B to 8B parameters, on both in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks, demonstrate that ProD substantially mitigates progress stagnation while enhancing both the success rates and task-completion efficiency of distilled SLM agents.

f1ecddc0e857.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly capable of acting in complex tool-use environments, yet they often fail to recognize when tasks are infeasible and no valid solution exists. Recent work has formalized this reliability gap as the problem of agentic abstention, and existing approaches typically optimize a model or agent harness against a fixed set of tasks, leading to limited generalization to unseen
takeaways: The resulting best harness transfers across 19 other LLMs, improving abstention accuracy by 15.3 percentage points on average without any model-specific optimization, and enabling smaller models to match the performance of more powerful models at an estimated 85% lower cost.

Recent work has formalized this reliability gap as the problem of agentic abstention, and existing approaches typically optimize a model or agent harness against a fixed set of tasks, leading to limited generalization to unseen failure modes.
We introduce HERA, a framework for harness-environment co-evolution for agentic abstention.

b4333b9e5b86.summary: One of the first steps of a research pipeline is generating ideas. Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate this step, but most of this work optimizes the quality of individual ideas, while overlooking diversity.
takeaways: In our work, we study document-grounded ideation, focusing on increasing the diversity of LLM generated ideas and ensuring they are high quality.
We show that our trained 8B model achieves higher creative utility (a measure combining quality and diversity) than Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-6 Astra on our contamination-free benchmark.
When a coding agent runs proof-of-concept experiments on the ideas, our model's success@k is comparable to Claude Opus 4.8's, so we see that the added diversity does not cost any executability.

49573a81893c.description: Image editing models produce impressive results for individual edits, but their quality often deteriorates over multiple editing turns. Each editing turn introduces small distribution shifts that accumulate over successive edits, creating a gap between the input distributions encountered during the editor's original…
49573a81893c.summary: Image editing models produce impressive results for individual edits, but their quality often deteriorates over multiple editing turns. Each editing turn introduces small distribution shifts that accumulate over successive edits, creating a gap between the input distributions encountered during the editor's original training and multi-turn inference.
takeaways: We address this challenge through a distillation objective that leverages a teacher image editor to provide a reliable training signal when the model operates on its own previous outputs.

Each editing turn introduces small distribution shifts that accumulate over successive edits, creating a gap between the input distributions encountered during the editor's original training and multi-turn inference.

We introduce an asymmetric conditioning scheme: while the student performs edits sequentially on its own outputs, the teacher remains anchored to the original clean image and receives a compound editing instruction.

For DeepSeek, it reduces table storage from 203GB to 51GB, leaving room for larger workloads when the table is kept on GPU.
We introduce Conditional Program (CP), a compressed representation that reconstructs only the rows an input requests.

Across 26 vision-language models, we find that top models largely solve documentation when the answer is text in frame, but are weak at reading measurements and at judging small parts and spatial relations, such as whether a tape measure leans.

The mechanism is geometric: the prompt's direct influence is diluted as the context grows, and relay --- continuation tokens passing on what earlier tokens read from the prompt --- can only add logarithmic factors.

8a02df2f9421.title: OverSeer: Multi-Agent World Models Beyond What Agents See
8a02df2f9421.author: Runjia Li, Kam Woh Ng, Minghao Chen, Junlin Han et al.
8a02df2f9421.description: Despite the success of video world models, extending them to multiple agents is difficult because it requires generating several agent-specific video streams that are consistent in time and between agents. To address this gap, we introduce OverSeer, a multi-agent world model that augments egocentric agent views with…
8a02df2f9421.summary: Despite the success of video world models, extending them to multiple agents is difficult because it requires generating several agent-specific video streams that are consistent in time and between agents. To address this gap, we introduce OverSeer, a multi-agent world model that augments egocentric agent views with auxiliary camera views.
takeaways: To address this gap, we introduce OverSeer, a multi-agent world model that augments egocentric agent views with auxiliary camera views.
We conclude that these fixed views provide a simple and efficient way to improve multi-agent world models.

We suggest that, by fixing the auxiliary views in space, they act as a proxy for a world-centric representation: Unlike the agents' views, which can change entirely due to a simple change in agent position, changes in the auxiliary views directly map to localized changes in the world state.

Doing so requires solving each task correctly while integrating the resulting answers into a coherent response. In this paper, we identify a fundamental limitation in this process, where models make substantially more errors…
6b14cf5ac8c6.summary: Modern language models are increasingly asked to handle several tasks within a single prompt. Doing so requires solving each task correctly while integrating the resulting answers into a coherent response.
takeaways: Across both open-weight models and the frontier model Claude Opus 5, our findings instead point to an implicit thinking budget underlying this effect.
In particular, under composition, models use substantially fewer tokens per task than in isolation, even when the full sequence remains well within the context window.
Tasks that require longer solution traces in isolation are consequently more fragile under composition, i.e., models make more errors on prompts containing these tasks.

8c91ef7505fa.title: PhysLDM: Latent Diffusion for High-Fidelity Deformable Simulation
8c91ef7505fa.author: Yu Zhang, Xudong Xu, Xingang Pan
8c91ef7505fa.description: Neural simulation of high-fidelity deformable bodies is a foundational challenge in computer graphics and physical AI. Long-horizon prediction for high-resolution 3D volumetric meshes is hard: autoregressive methods are prone to error accumulation, while direct multi-frame prediction at native resolution is…
8c91ef7505fa.summary: Neural simulation of high-fidelity deformable bodies is a foundational challenge in computer graphics and physical AI. Long-horizon prediction for high-resolution 3D volumetric meshes is hard: autoregressive methods are prone to error accumulation, while direct multi-frame prediction at native resolution is computationally prohibitive.
takeaways: Our experiments uncover a key modeling insight: complex deformable dynamics are often chaotic, and in this regime deterministic regression tends to produce non-physical averages, whereas diffusion better models their distribution.
Accordingly, we employ a latent diffusion model that effectively learns from chaotic data to generate physically plausible trajectories.
Meanwhile, it remains unclear whether deterministic regression or generative diffusion is the more suitable predictive paradigm.

c70e6a8188cf.title: PVBench: Quantifying Physical Plausibility in Video Generation with Object-Level Physical Measurements
c70e6a8188cf.author: Kaiwei Chen, Moran Li, Zhenye Gan, Yabiao Wang et al.
c70e6a8188cf.description: Recent video generation models produce visually compelling outputs, yet their physical plausibility remains poorly measured. Physical plausibility asks whether generated objects obey geometry, kinematics, dynamics, and conservation laws. Existing benchmarks rely on coarse visual-language model judgments or target…
c70e6a8188cf.summary: Recent video generation models produce visually compelling outputs, yet their physical plausibility remains poorly measured. Physical plausibility asks whether generated objects obey geometry, kinematics, dynamics, and conservation laws.
takeaways: Existing benchmarks rely on coarse visual-language model judgments or target embodied world models rather than video generation itself.
PVBench comprises 600 carefully crafted prompts, of which 30% involve physical embodied agents such as robot arms, humanoids, quadrupeds, and multi-agent systems.
Finally, we validate the agreement between automatic metrics and human judgments through human evaluation.

f8e876915a2a.title: FlowState: Execution State as Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
f8e876915a2a.author: Minghao Li, Bangyan Li, Zifan Wang, Yulong Li et al.
f8e876915a2a.description: Long-horizon tasks require LLM agents to continually draw on information from earlier interactions. However, retaining the full history increases context costs, while compressing it risks losing details needed later, and the relevance of historical information often becomes apparent as the task progresses. To address…
f8e876915a2a.summary: Long-horizon tasks require LLM agents to continually draw on information from earlier interactions. However, retaining the full history increases context costs, while compressing it risks losing details needed later, and the relevance of historical information often becomes apparent as the task progresses.
takeaways: Compared with a full-context baseline using the same DeepSeek-V4-Flash model, FlowState improves the average success rate on MemoryArena and the average pass rate on τ^3-Bench by 4.55 and 13.95 percentage points, respectively, while reducing total token consumption by 43.2% and 40.6%.

To address these challenges, we propose FlowState, which treats execution state as memory that can be retained and revisited across requests, unifying current decision-making with the reuse of historical information.
Together, these mechanisms enable agents to reassess prior decisions in light of new information and guide subsequent actions.

4ede92e1e453.title: Evaluating Agentic Capabilities Before Post-Training: An End-to-End Approach
4ede92e1e453.author: Jiarui Qin, Junjie Huang, Yunjia Xi, Di Yin et al.
4ede92e1e453.description: Agentic capabilities are increasingly important for modern LLMs, yet remain difficult to evaluate during pretraining. Existing approaches typically rely on static trajectory-derived tasks or likelihood-based proxies, which are lightweight but provide limited visibility into how base models behave in interactive…
4ede92e1e453.summary: Agentic capabilities are increasingly important for modern LLMs, yet remain difficult to evaluate during pretraining. Existing approaches typically rely on static trajectory-derived tasks or likelihood-based proxies, which are lightweight but provide limited visibility into how base models behave in interactive environments.
takeaways: We introduce ASAP (Agent Scaffold Adaptation for Pretraining Evaluation), a lightweight framework for eliciting and evaluating agentic behavior from pretrained base models on end-to-end tasks.
Our results suggest that end-to-end agent evaluation can complement conventional pretraining benchmarks by providing a practical diagnostic of interactive model behavior.
Across software-engineering and deep-research benchmarks, ASAP yields discriminative end-to-end performance across base models and pretraining checkpoints.

f22bbc2843f0.title: LLM2R: From Large Language Models to 3D Reassemblers
f22bbc2843f0.author: Zhouhan Zhong, Qiuhong Shen, Xingyi Yang, Jinyi Xu et al.
f22bbc2843f0.description: 3D part assembly aims to reconstruct a complete shape from a set of unassembled parts by predicting a rigid SE(3) transformation for each part. Because the placement of a part is rarely determined by its own geometry, the task demands reasoning over the entire part set, and existing methods, which rely on pairwise…
f22bbc2843f0.summary: 3D part assembly aims to reconstruct a complete shape from a set of unassembled parts by predicting a rigid SE(3) transformation for each part. Because the placement of a part is rarely determined by its own geometry, the task demands reasoning over the entire part set, and existing methods, which rely on pairwise relations or iterative generation and verification, scale poorly to objects with many parts.
takeaways: LLM2R therefore appends a block of learnable summary tokens after the last part: these tokens follow every part, so their states aggregate the whole assembly at a constant token cost, and a part-aware pose head fuses each part's states with them before predicting its rotation and translation.

LLM2R achieves the highest part accuracy and success rate on all three PartNet categories, the best rotation error, translation error, and part accuracy on PartNeXt, and the lowest translation error and fastest inference on Breaking Bad, where only a fracture-specialized method is more accurate.

Because the placement of a part is rarely determined by its own geometry, the task demands reasoning over the entire part set, and existing methods, which rely on pairwise relations or iterative generation and verification, scale poorly to objects with many parts.

2935eec587ce.title: Unsupervised Tool Evolution for Coding Agents in Data-Lake Analytics
2935eec587ce.author: Yuqing Yang, Yurong Liu, Deqing Fu, Manav Garg et al.
2935eec587ce.description: Coding agents can answer analytical questions over a data lake by discovering, cleaning, and joining the relevant data. However, they discard this work after each question and redo it from scratch for the next one. Tool evolution, which automatically builds and refines reusable tools across tasks, is a natural fit for…
2935eec587ce.summary: Coding agents can answer analytical questions over a data lake by discovering, cleaning, and joining the relevant data. However, they discard this work after each question and redo it from scratch for the next one.
takeaways: We propose TEAL (Tool Evolution for Analytics over data Lakes), which evolves a library of tools and usage skills for a given Worker agent without labels.
Two agents propose tools from complementary evidence, an Explorer from the data lake itself and a Critic from Worker trajectories.
We evaluate on KramaBench and LakeQA with four Worker LLMs under step budgets, which cap the number of steps the Worker may take per question.

1984a13a0ddb.title: Event-STVG: Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding for Long-Form Event Reasoning
1984a13a0ddb.author: Yizhe Zhang, Xujia Wang, Songqi Tang, Xujie Tang et al.
1984a13a0ddb.description: Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding (STVG) aims to jointly localize a target in space and time given a natural-language query. Despite continued advances, existing STVG benchmarks remain largely centered on localizing targets through instance-specific descriptions, leaving them largely decoupled from long-form reasoning…
1984a13a0ddb.summary: Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding (STVG) aims to jointly localize a target in space and time given a natural-language query. Despite continued advances, existing STVG benchmarks remain largely centered on localizing targets through instance-specific descriptions, leaving them largely decoupled from long-form reasoning increasingly emphasized in multimodal large language models (MLLMs).
takeaways: Despite continued advances, existing STVG benchmarks remain largely centered on localizing targets through instance-specific descriptions, leaving them largely decoupled from long-form reasoning increasingly emphasized in multimodal large language models (MLLMs).

In this paper, we introduce Event-STVG, a task that shifts STVG from locating what is described toward event-level reasoning by unifying long-form context, repeated-event reasoning, event localization, role inference, and multi-target grounding.
Experiments with state-of-the-art MLLMs reveal substantial difficulty, with the strongest model achieving only 5.4% m-vIoU at the 10-minute horizon.

63c4ea774a12.title: Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model
63c4ea774a12.author: Arash Ebrahim Abtahizadeh, Muna Aghamelu, Adil Ahmed, Juan C. Angeles Acuna et al.
63c4ea774a12.description: We introduce Muse Glimmer, an open-source 30B parameter causal language model with perception encoder, purpose-built for autonomous agentic tasks on consumer hardware. Muse Glimmer integrates multi-step reasoning, reliable tool use and failure recovery into a single model that runs locally on consumer devices without…
63c4ea774a12.summary: We introduce Muse Glimmer, an open-source 30B parameter causal language model with perception encoder, purpose-built for autonomous agentic tasks on consumer hardware. Muse Glimmer integrates multi-step reasoning, reliable tool use and failure recovery into a single model that runs locally on consumer devices without requiring cloud infrastructure.
takeaways: Muse Glimmer achieves state-of-the-art performance for its size class on agentic benchmarks, setting a new standard compared to the models of its size: Gemma4-31B and Qwen3.6-27B on tool use, multi-step planning, and agentic task completion.
Muse Glimmer integrates multi-step reasoning, reliable tool use and failure recovery into a single model that runs locally on consumer devices without requiring cloud infrastructure.
We release the model under the Apache 2.0 license to foster open-source development of capable, safe, local AI agents.

6bac73ae9245.title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
6bac73ae9245.author: Noam Rotstein, Yoad Tewel, Chen Tessler, Haggai Maron et al.
6bac73ae9245.description: Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion. Yet it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels: to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene. For instance, a video model can show a monkey jumping over a crossbar, but it cannot return that jump as replayable 3D…
6bac73ae9245.summary: Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion. Yet it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels: to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene.
takeaways: We instead keep 3D motion in a separate model that supports arbitrary skeletons, and connect it to a pretrained video model through a small set of cross-attention layers.
Our evaluations demonstrate that our model animates diverse rigs from text more faithfully than video-first pipelines, and its motion responds to the surrounding scene.
For instance, a video model can show a monkey jumping over a crossbar, but it cannot return that jump as replayable 3D motion placed in the 3D scene.

c32892111f0b.title: On the Limits of Scale: Inverse Scaling in Vision-Language Models
c32892111f0b.author: Rohit Saxena, Alessandro Suglia, Marek Rei, Pasquale Minervini
c32892111f0b.description: Scaling laws suggest that increasing model size, training data, and compute generally yields monotonic performance improvements. While this often holds at the aggregate level, we present systematic evidence that vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit inverse scaling at the subtask level: specific question categories on…
c32892111f0b.summary: Scaling laws suggest that increasing model size, training data, and compute generally yields monotonic performance improvements. While this often holds at the aggregate level, we present systematic evidence that vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit inverse scaling at the subtask level: specific question categories on which larger models perform worse than smaller counterparts within the same model family.
takeaways: We evaluate 19 models from four distinct model families across eight multimodal benchmarks (nine evaluation splits), answering 29,386 questions per model, 558,334 model-question evaluations in total.

While this often holds at the aggregate level, we present systematic evidence that vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit inverse scaling at the subtask level: specific question categories on which larger models perform worse than smaller counterparts within the same model family.
We identify 13 subtask-dataset pairs that show inverse scaling across multiple families, consistent with the phenomenon being task-driven rather than model-specific.

228d6181c906.title: SpecKCast: Spectral Kalman Forecasting for Diffusion Acceleration
228d6181c906.author: Javad Rajabi, Hakki Can Karaimer, David B. Lindell, Babak Taati et al.
228d6181c906.description: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) achieve high-fidelity image and video generation, but they suffer from substantial inference costs due to repeated transformer evaluations across many denoising steps. Feature caching reduces this cost by reusing features across denoising steps. Recent forecasting methods extend this idea…
228d6181c906.summary: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) achieve high-fidelity image and video generation, but they suffer from substantial inference costs due to repeated transformer evaluations across many denoising steps. Feature caching reduces this cost by reusing features across denoising steps.
takeaways: The filter tracks each coefficient's value and rate of change, and the transformer is evaluated only when the filter's forecast uncertainty exceeds a threshold.
We propose SpecKCast, a training-free method that forecasts the model output in the frequency domain.

Experiments on FLUX.1-dev, Qwen-Image, Wan2.1-14B, and HunyuanVideo show that SpecKCast achieves a better trade-off between acceleration and fidelity than existing caching and forecasting methods, reaching up to 6x speedup with less than 0.05 GiB of additional memory.

569b99be4ee7.title: Epi: Towards a Persistent, Self-Improving Agent for Autonomous Research
569b99be4ee7.author: Yue Huang, Zhangchen Xu, Xiaonan Luo, Zheyuan Liu et al.
569b99be4ee7.description: We present Épi, an autonomous research agent that sustains investigations across model sessions and evolves its methods through accumulated experience. Épi combines persistent research history, hierarchical memory, branching and independent review to maintain research continuity, learn from experiments, and explore…
569b99be4ee7.summary: Its experiments run across session boundaries, and a fixed verifier evaluates their outputs. Épi produced 120 record-setting results, comprising 20 numerical bound records across 12 families and 100 construction records across eight families. These include an approximately 84-fold narrower interval for the n-queens constant and a more than 3.6-million-fold narrower rigorous interval for the quartic Feigenbaum attract
takeaways: We extend this research process to algorithmic coding with Épi-turbo, a lightweight configuration that develops executable solvers for tasks including vehicle routing, scheduling and production planning.
These include an approximately 84-fold narrower interval for the n-queens constant and a more than 3.6-million-fold narrower rigorous interval for the quartic Feigenbaum attractor dimension.
Exact dual certificates establish that the Cohn-Elkies linear-programming bound cannot be sharp in dimensions 10 and 11.

9ad1b1532067.title: OmniCam: Omni-Camera Trajectory Generation via Geometry-Grounded Pose Token Learning
9ad1b1532067.author: Zhenyang Liu, Chenjie Cao, Yisu Zhang, Xuhui Zuo et al.
9ad1b1532067.description: Camera trajectories control viewpoint changes in video generation, scene reconstruction, and robotic perception. Generating them from language requires both scene geometry and target-aware framing. We introduce OmniCam, an autoregressive model that generates camera pose sequences from a single panorama and textual…
9ad1b1532067.summary: Camera trajectories control viewpoint changes in video generation, scene reconstruction, and robotic perception. Generating them from language requires both scene geometry and target-aware framing.
takeaways: We introduce OmniCam, an autoregressive model that generates camera pose sequences from a single panorama and textual trajectory descriptions.
On the reported OmniCaT evaluation, OmniCam reduces trajectory errors by 28--47% and collision rate by 65.8% relative to GenDoP retrained on OmniCaT.
Generating them from language requires both scene geometry and target-aware framing.

89a80ec03a10.title: λ_0: Scaling Open-World Egocentric Human Data for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
89a80ec03a10.author: humanoid Team
89a80ec03a10.description: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinated whole-body interaction with the physical world, yet collecting robot demonstrations at scale remains costly. Human demonstrations offer a scalable alternative, but existing egocentric human supervision often omits locomotion and posture, while embodiment differences and…
89a80ec03a10.summary: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinated whole-body interaction with the physical world, yet collecting robot demonstrations at scale remains costly. Human demonstrations offer a scalable alternative, but existing egocentric human supervision often omits locomotion and posture, while embodiment differences and controller dynamics hinder accurate end-effector execution.
takeaways: We expect this study to guide scalable whole-body human data collection toward humanoid foundation models for richer interaction with the physical world.
Building on this pipeline, we develop λ_0, a humanoid foundation model for whole-body loco-manipulation, with robot-aligned human demonstrations providing supervision for mid-training.

Human demonstrations offer a scalable alternative, but existing egocentric human supervision often omits locomotion and posture, while embodiment differences and controller dynamics hinder accurate end-effector execution.

d358384ce42f.summary: Computer-use agents are limited by the interfaces humans give them. An agent may type a spreadsheet cell by cell when a single line of code would do, or print all two thousand lines of a file through a shell to find one function.
takeaways: Both the interfaces and the knowledge of when to use each are built by hand, which cannot keep pace with new applications, workflows, and models.

Population-based evolution then selects which repositories to develop further by their performance on validation tasks the meta-agent never sees, favoring changes that generalize beyond the seen tasks.

On OSWorld V2, Agent S4, with Qwen3.8-27B and the evolved repository of interfaces, sets a new state of the art in open-source computer-use agents, reaching 21.3% binary score, 3.8 times the same model with fixed interfaces.

636deb7cdf06.summary: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models often exceed a single accelerator's memory capacity. Offloading experts to host memory creates a severe PCIe I/O bottleneck because data-dependent routing keeps transfers on the critical path.
takeaways: Under single-request inference, Specter achieves an average 1.50x (up to 1.88x) speedup in time per output token (TPOT) over the state-of-the-art system.
Specter makes memory-constrained, single-GPU MoE inference more practical on commodity hardware.
Offloading experts to host memory creates a severe PCIe I/O bottleneck because data-dependent routing keeps transfers on the critical path.

5601f92cef6d.summary: Multimodal rerankers are usually dedicated models: a vision-language model (VLM) is trained on retrieval data to score the candidates of a query. Scoring options is not specific to reranking.
takeaways: System One decision models such as Jev map a state and a typed question to one probability per option without generating text, and general models can make such decisions with little or no training.
On MMEB-V2 image retrieval, this choice scores 5.4 to 7.3 hit@1 above a yes/no question per candidate, and the yes/no question falls below the first stage.
Reranking is one such decision, with the query and its candidates as the state and the candidates as the options.

While existing models can synthesize visually stunning time-lapses of paintings being created or "unpainted," they largely treat the creative process as a black box.
takeaways: While existing models can synthesize visually stunning time-lapses of paintings being created or "unpainted," they largely treat the creative process as a black box.
Extensive benchmarking demonstrates the efficacy of our approach.

Current conditioning mechanisms are either too rigid, relying on static geometric cues like Canny edges or depth maps, or too holistic, utilizing simple scalar progress variables that offer no localized control.

The scarcity of contact-rich bimanual manipulation data and the increased complexity of coordinating contacts make developing a generalist bimanual tracker particularly challenging.
takeaways: The scarcity of contact-rich bimanual manipulation data and the increased complexity of coordinating contacts make developing a generalist bimanual tracker particularly challenging.
DONIC combines proximal policy optimization with behavioral cloning in a feedback loop that recycles verified successful executions into training demonstrations.
An object-centered per-hand reward maintains object-motion feedback while supervising each hand according to its reference contact role.

Across 10 open model lineages, post-training standardizes replies to every informal cue, yet after adjusting for how likely each reply already was, the DPO update still favours matching British and Australian spelling over AAE and Singlish on 10 lineages, and models still produce AAE features when asked.

We assess performance and generalization using three-level validation losses and gameplay benchmarks from in-corpus worlds to unseen worlds.
Our 120 training configurations span four model sizes from 0.8B to 27B, six data budgets from 50 to 1,600 hours, and five mixtures ranging from Minecraft-only data to diverse multi-world corpora.

Across five spatial-reasoning benchmarks, SpatialBrain improves on direct answers from the same backbone on four and ties on the fifth.
Component comparisons, experience-coverage curves, and traced resource decisions characterize how the framework accumulates and uses these resources.

takeaways: We take the context and the teacher's answer as input, and generate the reasoning trace ourselves, in the style of the student's own model family.
Some frontier teams have closed that route for their own models: what comes back is an answer, or a short summary, without the detailed reasoning trace behind it.
That is a little ironic: they were themselves built on distilling human knowledge, and distilling an open-source model is still entirely routine; the restriction applies to their own outputs alone.

takeaways: Loops appear natively in Qwen, Llama, and Gemini agents and become far more common once the agent's history is compressed to fit its context window.
DeLoop builds on a simple observation: the agent's own rollout can provide the supervision needed to learn from its loops.
DeLoop learns from these pairs through direct preference optimization and does not require task rewards, gold answers, or LLM judges.

1cc9e8737f33.summary: Autonomous agents can increasingly propose ideas, modify code, and run experiments, creating an opportunity to accelerate scientific discovery using teams of collaborative AI researchers. To escape local minima in the discovery, we propose to encourage orthogonal exploration by constructing the team using agents with varying expertise.
takeaways: We demonstrate the effectiveness of this design by deploying the team to search for linear attention architectures, where it outperforms GDN2 at 1.3B scale on language modeling, common-sense reasoning, and synthetic and real-world retrieval tasks.
To escape local minima in the discovery, we propose to encourage orthogonal exploration by constructing the team using agents with varying expertise.
These results suggest that sustained autonomous discovery depends not only on stronger agents, but also on who explores, what they remember, and how research effort is allocated.

20a259028135.title: The bridge to agent-scale Git infrastructure
20a259028135.author: Eleanor White
20a259028135.description: We moved a copy of 99.99999% of GitHub's repositories to Azure. Here's how per-reference quorums will bring over the rest, and how object storage lets reads scale independently. The post The bridge to agent-scale Git infrastructure appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
20a259028135.summary: Over the past year, while Git traffic grew exponentially, 99.99999% of the Git repositories on GitHub began living in two places at once: our own data centers and Azure. The rest are among the busiest on the platform, and they’re held back by just one thing: a 25ms round trip.
takeaways: While we had prototyped new architectural approaches for scaling Git on cloud infrastructure, changing the storage architecture and the hosting platform at the same time, under that growth, carried too much risk.

How we got here The timing and shape of the move were driven by the agentic shift: rapidly growing traffic, a hard ceiling on the power capacity of our data centers and the surrounding geographical region, and physical supply chain constraints.

In an earlier blog post , we laid out the two principles behind our next-generation storage architecture: Minimize coordination Decouple storage from compute In this post, we’ll look at the immediate bridge between our old design and our new one.

8e385112441d.summary: Uniform diffusion language models (UDLMs) generate text by iteratively denoising sequences of ordinary vocabulary tokens, any of which may be corrupted and subsequently revised. During training, UDLMs must denoise from a context that may itself be unreliable, whereas masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) always condition on a clean context.
takeaways: Finally, we study different loop-count distributions and find that sampling smaller loop counts more frequently during training improves inference efficiency: on downstream tasks, this strategy uses 12% fewer loops than uniform loop-count sampling without degrading accuracy.
During training, UDLMs must denoise from a context that may itself be unreliable, whereas masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) always condition on a clean context.
This challenging training objective makes UDLMs more FLOP-intensive to train than MDLMs, but it yields stronger downstream reasoning performance.

328e6a30c271.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) robustness is commonly summarized by aggregate task success, which obscures how individual executions change under distribution shifts and where failures emerge in long-horizon tasks. We introduce RoboCasa-Shift, a diagnostic robustness benchmark built on RoboCasa365 that combines controlled single-factor shifts, matched clean-perturbed rollouts in which each pair shares the same underlyi
takeaways: We evaluate GR00T N1.5 on four long-horizon tasks that pass a predefined clean-performance gate under four perturbation factors and three calibrated severity levels, including conditions that drive the evaluated policy to complete task failure, totaling 1,040 formal rollouts.

Our findings suggest that VLA robustness should be viewed as a multi-dimensional property of execution rather than a single end-to-end performance measure, motivating evaluation protocols that jointly capture outcome degradation, paired outcome sensitivity, and failure progression.

We introduce RoboCasa-Shift, a diagnostic robustness benchmark built on RoboCasa365 that combines controlled single-factor shifts, matched clean-perturbed rollouts in which each pair shares the same underlying settings and differs only in the target shift, and simulator-grounded stage-aware diagnostics.

In this paper, we present a controlled comparison of data-level and training-level interventions for navigating the capability-privacy tradeoff on synthetic medical records with canaries to probe for leakage.
takeaways: Overall, these results highlight privacy-aware rewriting as a promising direction for achieving a more favorable trade-off between capabilities and empirical privacy compared to other training-level methods, and our evaluation framework supports comparisons of future models and methods.

In this paper, we present a controlled comparison of data-level and training-level interventions for navigating the capability-privacy tradeoff on synthetic medical records with canaries to probe for leakage.
Relative to naive paraphrasing, privacy-aware rewriting improves privacy protection across a variety of different rewriting models.

217a5f6b1faa.title: Hidden Messages Between Diffusion Language Model Agents: Causal Evidence for Latent Communication
217a5f6b1faa.author: Alan-Barsag Gazzaev, Alexey Gavrilov, Sergey Muravyov, Ilya Makarov
217a5f6b1faa.description: Diffusion language models form answers through a sequence of revisable continuous states, but multi-agent systems usually discard those states and make agents communicate only after decoding text. We ask whether one independent diffusion trajectory can pass a compact hidden message into another and, crucially, whether…
217a5f6b1faa.summary: Diffusion language models form answers through a sequence of revisable continuous states, but multi-agent systems usually discard those states and make agents communicate only after decoding text. We ask whether one independent diffusion trajectory can pass a compact hidden message into another and, crucially, whether the receiver uses what that message means.
takeaways: These experiments provide causal evidence for continuous hidden communication between diffusion-LM agents and show that when information is transferred can matter more than how many times agents exchange it.
We ask whether one independent diffusion trajectory can pass a compact hidden message into another and, crucially, whether the receiver uses what that message means.
In Hidden Messages, a sender compresses its denoising state into four signed dense vectors; the receiver consumes them while retaining its own context, canvas, and trajectory.

5d26b822dea6.summary: Deep research systems iteratively plan, gather evidence, synthesize, and revise, making end-to-end latency a key bottleneck for interactive use. Almost all production systems are built on autoregressive (AR) language models and inherit left-to-right decoding in planning and long-form writing.
takeaways: Holding the agentic scaffold, retrieval code, prompts, and evaluation fixed, we swap the backbone between an open diffusion model and a comparable AR model.

We present DiffResearch, an open multi-agent deep research framework that places a diffusion language model (dLLM) at the core of every stage, and measure how a diffusion backbone changes latency and report quality.
Almost all production systems are built on autoregressive (AR) language models and inherit left-to-right decoding in planning and long-form writing.

43bc44ba1aa7.title: Quant-Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Quantitative Trading Research
43bc44ba1aa7.author: Houde Qian, Zheng Jiang, Wenyi Li, Chenxi Xu et al.
43bc44ba1aa7.description: Quantitative research is an iterative loop: a researcher proposes a market hypothesis, implements it as an executable signal, tests it on historical data, and decides what to keep. Existing benchmarks score formulas, code, or individual trading decisions, leaving open whether large language models (LLMs) can complete…
43bc44ba1aa7.summary: Quantitative research is an iterative loop: a researcher proposes a market hypothesis, implements it as an executable signal, tests it on historical data, and decides what to keep. Existing benchmarks score formulas, code, or individual trading decisions, leaving open whether large language models (LLMs) can complete this loop and produce strategies that work beyond the research period.
takeaways: Existing benchmarks score formulas, code, or individual trading decisions, leaving open whether large language models (LLMs) can complete this loop and produce strategies that work beyond the research period.
We evaluate nine frontier models, among which GPT-6 Astra scores highest; yet no model beats the equal-weight market in 2024.
We introduce Quant-Arena, a benchmark and public leaderboard for end-to-end quantitative research on real A-share market data.

b74f7461929f.title: ToM2Vec: Continuous Theory-of-Mind Tokens for Multi-Agent Coordination
b74f7461929f.author: Nithin Sivakumaran, Ali Payani, Hyunji Lee, Mohit Bansal et al.
b74f7461929f.description: Forming an accurate theory-of-mind (ToM) is key to successful multi-agent collaboration and requires reasoning under uncertainty to capture multiple possible partner states. This is hard to do in the text representation space native to large language model (LLM) agents, which more easily describe a single partner…
b74f7461929f.summary: Forming an accurate theory-of-mind (ToM) is key to successful multi-agent collaboration and requires reasoning under uncertainty to capture multiple possible partner states. This is hard to do in the text representation space native to large language model (LLM) agents, which more easily describe a single partner state.
takeaways: This is hard to do in the text representation space native to large language model (LLM) agents, which more easily describe a single partner state.
To address this challenge, we introduce ToM2Vec, which learns to form abstract theories-of-mind in a rich latent space via a fixed budget of continuous reasoning tokens.
At test-time, ToM tokens are generated by each agent and act as conditioners for that agent's thoughts and actions.

28666c0ad99b.title: Design Anything, Design at Scale
28666c0ad99b.author: Xuchao Ren, Siyuan Feng, Jing Huang, Yanhua Yao et al.
28666c0ad99b.description: As multimodal resources are transformed into media outputs, agentic AI is expected to stay aligned with design intent over long horizons. Designers follow briefs specifying goals, constraints, and deliverables, with later work building on earlier decisions. Recent work reuses design experience across tasks, yet…
28666c0ad99b.summary: As multimodal resources are transformed into media outputs, agentic AI is expected to stay aligned with design intent over long horizons. Designers follow briefs specifying goals, constraints, and deliverables, with later work building on earlier decisions.
takeaways: We introduce Design Anything, a graph-based harness that preserves design intent outside the model and binds deliverables to the workflow steps that produce them through an intent-execution graph.

With the LLM held fixed, Design Anything satisfies 85.0% and 92.5% of the brief's factual constraints with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash High and GPT-5.6 Sol High, respectively, exceeding the strongest same-model baselines by 15.4% and 14.4%.
Professional designers also prefer its complete deliverable sets over those of same-model baselines in a blind evaluation.

d33ccf89dda0.title: Retrieval Augmented Generation Compositionality
d33ccf89dda0.author: Ido Levy, Segev Shlomov, Leshem Choshen
d33ccf89dda0.description: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) grounds large language models in external knowledge. Modern pipelines combine embedding, chunking, retrieval, reranking, query augmentation, context compression, and agentic verification, yet these techniques are typically evaluated one at a time. It remains unclear whether their…
d33ccf89dda0.summary: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) grounds large language models in external knowledge. Modern pipelines combine embedding, chunking, retrieval, reranking, query augmentation, context compression, and agentic verification, yet these techniques are typically evaluated one at a time.
takeaways: Modern pipelines combine embedding, chunking, retrieval, reranking, query augmentation, context compression, and agentic verification, yet these techniques are typically evaluated one at a time.

First, individually strong techniques from different phases of a RAG pipeline do not necessarily compose: three retrieval techniques predict a +47% combined improvement but deliver only +17% when used together.

It remains unclear whether their isolated gains survive composition, whether retrieval quality and answer faithfulness favor the same design choices, and whether conclusions from small corpora hold at large scale.

e26b258d01b9.title: From RL Papers to Framework Code: Inclusion and Review in Seven Open-Source Training Frameworks

e26b258d01b9.description: Practitioners use reinforcement learning methods for language models through training frameworks, so a method that a framework includes is one configuration change away for its users. We measure how often this happens. We trace seven open-source frameworks for RL post-training through their commit histories and link…
e26b258d01b9.summary: Practitioners use reinforcement learning methods for language models through training frameworks, so a method that a framework includes is one configuration change away for its users. We trace seven open-source frameworks for RL post-training through their commit histories and link them to 6,939 screened arXiv papers from January 2025 to June 2026.
takeaways: We trace seven open-source frameworks for RL post-training through their commit histories and link them to 6,939 screened arXiv papers from January 2025 to June 2026.
Both gaps hold without papers from the companies that maintain the frameworks, while code release was equally common in both groups.
Of 1,598 papers that propose a general RL training method, 37 reached at least one framework.
